extraction.name: OpenThoughts3-1.2M
extraction.description: A state-of-the-art open-source dataset for training reasoning models, containing 1.2 million question-response pairs across math, code, and science domains, generated through a systematic pipeline involving question sourcing, filtering, deduplication, multiple answer sampling, and teacher model annotation.
extraction.creator: Etash Guha, Ryan Marten, Sedrick Keh, Negin Raoof, Georgios Smymis, Hritik Bansal, Marianna Nezhurina, Jean Mercat, Trung Vu, Zayne Sprague, Ashima Suvama, Benjamin Feuer, Liangyu Chen, Zaid Khan, Eric Frankel, Sachin Grover, Caroline Choi, Niklas Muennighoff, Shiye Su, Wanjia Zhao, John Yang, Shreyas Pimpalgaonkar, Kartik Sharma, Charlie Cheng-Jie Ji, Yichuan Deng, Sarah Pratt, Vivek Ramanujan, Jon Saad-Falcon, Jeffrey Li, Achal Dave, Alon Albalak, Kushal Arora, Blake Wulfe, Chinmay Hegde, Greg Durrett, Sewoong Oh, Mohit Bansal, Saadia Gabriel, Aditya Grover, Kai-Wei Chang, Vaishaal Shankar, Aaron Gokaslan, Mike A. Merrill, Tatsunori Hashimoto, Yejin Choi, Jenia Jitsev, Reinhard Heckel, Maheswaran Sathiamoorthy, Alexandros G. Dimakis, Ludwig Schmidt
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data is collected through a pipeline involving question sourcing from various datasets (e.g., StackExchange, OpenCodeReasoning, OpenMath-2-Math), filtering questions using LLM-based methods, deduplication, sampling multiple answers per question from a teacher model, and mixing questions from top-performing sources.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data includes questions from sources such as StackExchange (CodeGolf, Physics), OpenCodeReasoning, OpenMath-2-Math, NuminaMath, Organic Chemistry PDFs, and other synthetic and non-synthetic datasets.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data manipulation includes filtering questions based on difficulty or response length using LLMs (e.g., GPT-4o-mini), deduplication (exact or fuzzy), and sampling multiple answers per question (e.g., 16x).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Preprocessing involves decontamination against evaluation benchmarks using Indel similarity and N-gram-based methods to remove contaminated samples, and filtering out incomplete or low-quality entries.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations (responses) are generated by querying a teacher model (QwQ-32B) multiple times per question to produce reasoning traces, with no answer filtering applied as it did not improve performance.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: LLM APIs (e.g., for QwQ-32B, DeepSeek-R1) and custom tooling for verification and filtering.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No significant improvement was found from answer filtering methods (e.g., verification, majority consensus), so all generated responses are used without conversion or disagreement analysis.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4.1-nano, GPT-4.1-mini, QwQ-32B, DeepSeek-R1, Phi-4-reasoning-plus
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Datasets and models are available on openthoughts.ai and Hugging Face, with ongoing updates as part of the OpenThoughts project.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to demystify SFT data curation for reasoning models and provide open-source resources to advance research in AI reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Biases may arise from the sources of questions (e.g., competitive programming forums, academic texts) and the teacher model's outputs, but specific biases are not discussed.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include not exploring reinforcement learning datasets, staged SFT, or curriculum learning; potential overthinking in models; and generalization deficits as shown in Alice in Wonderland evaluations.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Use cases include Training, Testing, and Validation for reasoning models in math, code, and science domains; usage guidelines emphasize open-source availability and benchmarking on tasks like AIME, LiveCodeBench, and GPQA.
